# `s2_security_groups` — version 1.0

Source: `presets/security-group-models/s2-security-groups.satz`

## Purpose

The S2 security group model: S1's five admin groups plus a distinct
NETWORK ADMINS group, and the org-level grants split accordingly. In S1 the
network authority is folded into project-admins (compute.networkAdmin,
compute.xpnAdmin — "Hybrid Connectivity administrators … Network
administrators" in their description); S2 carves it out so a network team
can own VPCs, Shared VPC, firewalls, DNS and connectivity without the
project-admin power over everything else, and project-admins lose exactly
those two network roles. Everything else is S1 unchanged.

Groups and grants in ONE file (typed sections beside the estate's own):
use "presets/security-group-models/s2-security-groups.satz"

To adopt groups that already exist in the tenant:
satz adopt <estate> --only google_cloud_identity_group --execute
Memberships are deliberately NOT part of this pack: presets define groups,
humans grant membership.

Required from the estate: customer_domain, svc_iac_account, infra_project_name

## Notes

<!-- notes:start — hand-written, kept across `satz doc-packs` -->

### S1 vs S2 — who holds what

| Group | S1 | S2 |
|---|---|---|
| `gcp-organization-admins` | org/folder/project admin, org-role admin, org-policy admin, project creator, support, billing user | unchanged |
| `gcp-project-admins` | day-2 project ownership (`owner`, project IAM admin, tag admin, SA creator, bigquery/pubsub admin, logging/monitoring admin) **+ `compute.networkAdmin`, `compute.xpnAdmin`** | the same **minus the two network roles** |
| `gcp-network-admins` | — | `compute.networkAdmin`, `compute.xpnAdmin`, `compute.securityAdmin`, `dns.admin`, `networkconnectivity.hubAdmin`, `networkmanagement.admin`, `compute.viewer`, `resourcemanager.folderViewer`, `logging.viewer`, `monitoring.viewer` |
| `gcp-security-admins` | org-policy admin, folder IAM admin, SCC admin, security reviewer, cloudasset viewer, logging/monitoring | unchanged |
| `gcp-security-viewers` | `viewer` + org viewer, security reviewer, cloudasset viewer, log/monitoring viewers | unchanged |
| `gcp-billing-admins` | org viewer, billing admin, billing creator | unchanged |

**Why the split:** Shared VPC host projects, firewall policies and hybrid
connectivity are org-wide blast radius; S1 hands them to every project admin.
S2 gives them to one team without `owner` or any IAM-admin role — a network
admin can wire a project but cannot grant anyone anything. `compute.securityAdmin`
is included because firewall *policies* (hierarchical rules) need it and
`compute.networkAdmin` alone cannot edit them; `dns.admin` because private
zones and peering are network work in practice.

### Roles and teams — who sits where

| Group | Role in the organization | Typical people |
|---|---|---|
| `gcp-organization-admins` | Owns the organization: folder tree, org policies, org-level IAM, custom roles. The break-glass tier — a handful of people, ideally never used day to day. | Cloud platform lead, the IaC/landing-zone owners |
| `gcp-project-admins` | Day-2 operation of workload projects: project IAM, service accounts, data/messaging services, logging and monitoring. Cannot change the org or its policies. | Platform engineers, application-team leads who run their own projects |
| `gcp-network-admins` (S2) | Everything that connects: VPCs and subnets, Shared VPC host/service wiring, firewall rules and hierarchical policies, Cloud DNS, VPN/Interconnect/NCC hubs, network diagnostics. No project ownership, no IAM. | Network / connectivity team, often the on-prem network team's cloud arm |
| `gcp-security-admins` | Sets and enforces guardrails: org policies, SCC configuration, folder IAM, log routing. Reads everything for investigations. | Security engineering / SOC leads |
| `gcp-security-viewers` | Read-only across the organization for audit and review; SCC viewer; compliance evidence (`report-compliance` needs exactly this — cloudasset viewer included). | Auditors, compliance, security analysts, external assessors |
| `gcp-billing-admins` | Billing accounts, budgets, cost allocation, procurement. | Finance / FinOps, the commercial owner of the contract |

### Which model — a team-shape decision

**S1** fits when one platform team does both the project administration and
the networking — typically up to the low tens of projects, one or two hub
VPCs, and the same two or three engineers touching both. The network roles
ride along in project-admins because the people are the same; a separate
group would only add membership overhead.

**S2** fits as soon as network and project administration are different
people — a dedicated network/connectivity team, Shared VPC with many service
projects, hierarchical firewall policies, hybrid connectivity to an on-prem
estate, or a regulator who asks for separation of duties. The network team
gets org-wide reach over connectivity and nothing else; project admins keep
their projects but can no longer re-wire the network. Choose S2 on day 0 when
that team split is already visible on the org chart: moving from S1 to S2
later is a pack swap plus re-adopting the new group, but every project admin
silently loses two roles at that apply — announce it.

Both are typed packs for a top-level `use`; the two-file S1 spelling
(`s1-group-definitions` + `s1-group-permissions` under their resource types)
stays for the estates on it and is content-identical to `s1_security_groups`.

**Memberships** are never in a pack: adopt the groups (`satz adopt --only
google_cloud_identity_group --execute`), then humans add members in the
console or with gcloud.
